title: An Approximation Algorithm for Graph Label Selection
claim: A vertex with high degree can be split by adding an infinite-weight auxiliary vertex, reducing its degree without changing the structure.
layout: 2 panels side by side, before-to-after left-to-right, labeled tree edges
description: Two black-and-white line drawings of rooted trees sit side by side. In the left panel, a circular root vertex labeled 0 hangs from a parent edge r. It has four child edges labeled a, b, c and d, each ending in a triangle subtree numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4, with an ellipsis between 1 and 2. In the right panel, the same root keeps its parent edge r and its children 1 and 2 with edges a and b. Its third edge, labeled with infinity, leads to a new circular vertex X. X holds subtrees 3 and 4 through edges c and d. The root's degree drops from four children to three. The eye goes first to the circles and the infinity label on the right. There is no color. The figure uses plain math notation.
caption: Decreasing degree by 1 by introducing a new vertex $X$ with $\infty$ edge weight.
abstract: In the graph label selection problem, one is given an $n$-vertex graph and a budget $k$, and seeks to select $k$ vertices whose labels enable accurate prediction of the labels on the remaining vertices. This problem formalizes distilling a small representative set from the whole graph. We present the first $\tilde{O}(\log^{1.5} n)$-approximation algorithm for graph label selection under the standard budget constraint. Prior work either relies on resource augmentation, allowing substantially more than $k$ labeled vertices, or consists primarily of heuristics without provable guarantees. Finally, we demonstrate that practical heuristic variants of our algorithm scale to significantly larger graphs than previous methods, while essentially retaining their quality.
